newsitem.title: JAPAN: No evidence of squeeze in LME copper stocks--Bagri.
newsitem.headline: No evidence of squeeze in LME copper stocks--Bagri.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) chairman Raj Bagri said on Tuesday that there was no evidence at the moment of a squeeze in LME copper stocks.
Asked at a news conference if someone was cornering the stocks, Bagri said: "There's absolutely no evidence of that as far as we can see at the moment."
"These are normal trade movements," he said, adding that copper consumption is strong and some producers are experiencing difficulties.
"There's no doubt that copper consumption is going extremely well," he said.
The LME chairman is currently visiting Tokyo to hold a seminar on the LME.
Bagri also noted difficulties this year at new copper production facilities such as Cyprus Amax Minerals Co's majority-owned El Abra complex and Kennecott Copper's Garfield smelter.
"They're having quite a lot of teething problems," he said, adding that an expected increase in production has not materialised as quickly as expected.
LME Chief Executive David King said it was the LME's understanding that quite a lot of the copper recently removed from LME warehouses has gone to or is en route to China.

Bagri added, however, that this was a supposition, and that he was also hearing that a large volume of copper was moving from Europe to the United States and from the LME copper warehouse in Long Beach, California to the Far East.
He also said there was talk of further stocks moving out of the warehouses in the future.
LME warehouse stocks of copper have fallen sharply in recent weeks, to 145,825 tonnes on October 28 from 275,775 tonnes on September 5.
